Details

Baseline = the STEP capsule used in pairs_v2 (500 bar ³He, 0.6 mm Al + 0.9 mm CFRP) with the standard MM window (40 µm Mylar, 50 µm Kapton, 9 µm Cu). Upgrade = 2 bar ³He in the 12 µm aluminised-mylar rod-cage cell of x17_facility_search/vessel_design, and a drift window of two aluminised mylar foils (outer for gas containment, inner for HV; 12 µm each assumed). Rough estimate: no acceptance, energy-loss or range changes.

Details

Scripts: scripts/scattering_geometry.py (ray tracing), scripts/make_scattering_upgrade_figs.py (matplotlib versions of these figures), scripts/make_scattering_upgrade_deck.py (this note).

Details

Baseline components (x/X₀ %): ³He gas 0.075, Al capsule (0.6 mm barrel, dome) 1.142, CFRP wrap (0.9 mm) 0.397, Air (≈24 cm) 0.091, Cu cathode (9 µm) 0.072, Kapton (50 µm) 0.020, Mylar (40 µm) 0.016, Drift gas (30 mm ArIso) 0.032. Upgrade: ³He gas 0.0012, Al coating (2×40 nm) 0.0001, Mylar skin (12 µm) 0.0054, Air (≈24 cm) 0.0843, their Al coating 0.0002, 2 window foils: mylar (12 µm each) 0.0098, Drift gas (30 mm ArIso) 0.0322. The normal-incidence barrel-only budget in angular_resolution_note.md is 1.26%; the ray-traced average is 1.81% upstream because tracks cross the wall obliquely and ~25% leave through the dome or neck.

4

Details

Baseline total = measured Geant4 median ψ(KE) from the 'first' estimator in geant4_response.json (X17 + IPC, e⁻ and e⁺ combined), times a 1% factor for the drift gas, which that estimator does not contain. Upgrade total = the same curve times the Highland ratio θ₀(x_upgrade)/θ₀(x_baseline upstream). Bands apportion the total by each component's share of x/X₀ (scattering variances add). At X17 energies KE⁻+KE⁺ ≈ 19.6 MeV, so one leg is always ≤ 9.8 MeV; the soft leg sets the opening-angle resolution. Below 2 MeV the response table is too coarse to show.

5

Details

Acceptance: four flat arms at 250 mm, active area 399 mm tangential × 360 mm along the beam, centred on the origin; pinwheel shifts ignored. The 'barrel' is |z_exit| ≤ 20 mm. This answers whether the budget is a side-exit-only estimate: it is not, and the nose and neck (solid Al, r = 3.5 mm) matter because roughly a quarter of the accepted tracks cross them.

6

Details

Method: sample X17 pairs at rest (E* = 20.58 MeV), tilt each leg by ψ drawn from P(ψ|KE) of the 'first' estimator in pairs_v2, multiplied by θ₀(x_case)/θ₀(x_baseline upstream) at that KE. This keeps the measured non-Gaussian tails. The baseline reproduces the note's σ68 = 15.5°. Sensitivity: with a 7 µm rolled-Al permeation layer on the cell skin (instead of 2×40 nm), x/X₀ rises 0.133% → 0.143% and σ68 3.8° → 3.9°. Not modelled: acceptance changes (the 300 mm cell has a longer vertex distribution than the 60 mm capsule), energy loss and range of soft legs through the old wall, rods and seam of the cell (≈ 9% of azimuth), IPC background.

Appendix: ⁴He instead of air, plus two foils, halves it again — σ68 3.8° → 2.5°

The air gap (0.084%) becomes 0.005% of ⁴He plus 0.010% of foil; the 30 mm drift gas is then the largest term

7

Details

Scenario: the 24 cm between target and MM is a ⁴He volume (ρ = 0.166 mg/cm³, X₀ = 5.7×10⁵ cm), closed by two further 12 µm aluminised-mylar foils (one at each end of the bag). Peak height ×0.50 → ×0.60, FWHM 11° → 8°. The remaining budget is 0.064% X₀, of which 51% is the drift gas, so removing the bag volume altogether (operating the MM in the target vacuum or gas volume) would be the only way to go further. The bag foils must withstand the pressure difference to air; the inner window foil holds the HV.

Caveats and next steps

The scattering we had at n_TOF was large; at low pressure it becomes a question about the air

What this does not rule out

• The upgrade acceptance is not modelled: a 300 mm cell has a much longer vertex distribution than the 60 mm capsule, and low-energy legs the old wall stopped would now reach the MM.

• Foil thicknesses are assumptions (12 µm window foils; 40 nm Al coatings). A 7 µm Al permeation layer on the skin costs σ68 3.8° → 3.9°.

• Rods and seam (≈ 9% of azimuth) scatter far more than the facets and are ignored.

• Scaling a measured table by the mean material ratio ignores that individual tracks cross very different thicknesses.

Decisions this points at

1. Go to the low-pressure mylar cell: it removes 83% of the baseline budget.

2. Choose the MM window by what holds HV, not by the foil stack: two mylar foils cost 0.01% X₀.

3. Then the air is 63% of what remains: decide whether a ⁴He bag (σ68 → 2.5°) is worth the extra foils and engineering.

4. Re-run with a full Geant4 simulation of the cell geometry to replace the scaling.
